subject: physics
title: Superposition and Young's Double Slit
welcome_lead: Stack waves on each other and decode the bright fringes of Young's classic experiment.
meta_desc: A-Level Waves adventure on superposition, interference and double-slit fringe spacing.
final_note: Path difference of n lambda gives a bright fringe; (n+½) lambda gives a dark one.

concepts.def: Resultant displacement is sum of individual ones.
w = lambda D / s for Young's slits.
Difference in distance from each source.

walkthroughs.body_html: When two waves overlap, total displacement equals the vector sum. Identical waves in phase double in amplitude (constructive); pi out of phase cancel (destructive).
Two coherent slits separated by s, screen distance D, light wavelength lambda. Bright fringes appear with spacing w = lambda D / s. Greater D or smaller s widens fringes.
Bright: path difference = n lambda. Dark: path difference = (n + 0.5) lambda. n is an integer (0,1,2,.).
